key_insight: CoopEval reveals that recent LLMs—even when using enhanced reasoning—tend to defect in single-shot social dilemmas, and provides the first systematic benchmark to evaluate mechanisms that aim to sustain cooperation among LLM agents. This enables direct comparison of models and intervention strategies in mixed-motive settings.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in evaluating and comparing how well LLM agents cooperate (or fail to) in social dilemmas and which mechanisms (e.g., communication, repetition, commitment) actually sustain cooperation.
method: Introduce CoopEval: a benchmark suite of canonical social-dilemma games and standardized evaluation protocols for LLM agents.
Systematically evaluate recent LLMs (with and without reasoning modes) on cooperation metrics across single-shot and extended interactions.
Compare the effectiveness of a variety of cooperation-sustaining mechanisms to identify what increases or fails to increase cooperative behavior.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners and safety researchers quantify cooperation failures in LLM-based agents and choose or design mechanisms that better align multi-agent interactions with cooperative, safe outcomes. Facilitates more reliable deployment of autonomous agents in mixed-motive environments.
visual_elements: Bar chart: cooperation rate by model (and with/without reasoning) for single-shot dilemmas

paper_title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
paper_authors: Emanuel Tewolde, Xiao Zhang, David Guzman Piedrahita, Vincent Conitzer, Zhijing Jin
